view.info.title: Information
view.info.help: This page sums up how the game works: rules, drop rates, experience and credits. The rates shown are read straight from the data files, exactly like a real draw.
info.toc.title: Contents
info.toc.label: Page contents
info.hint.label: Show the explanation
info.sets.title: Expansions and releases
info.sets.intro: Every expansion has a release day. A popup announces it once, at the first load after that day: you can read it again here, whenever you want.
info.sets.help: The dates are the game ones, in UTC days. An expansion that is not released yet already shows in the booster picker with its 3D model, but it cannot be opened and its cards do not join the collection.
info.details.title: Panel help
info.details.intro: The detailed explanations of the settings, the profile and the trader. Every panel also opens them from its small information icon, without leaving the screen.
info.how.title: How does it work?
info.how.intro: MineCards is a collection game. Your account, your collection and your statistics stay in this browser: nothing is sent to a server.
info.how.step1: Every day you get 3 free boosters. Bonus boosters can also be credited by promo codes and distributions.
info.how.step2: Pick an extension and open a booster: its 5 cards are drawn and stored immediately, before the animation.
info.how.step3: Reveal the cards one by one, then read the summary. The booster code (minecards:…) lets you share the opening.
info.how.step4: The cards you get join your collection (duplicates stack up) and feed the statistics.
info.how.godpack: Rarely, a booster can be a “god pack”: all 5 of its cards are then full art printings, whatever their rarity.
info.minepick.title: Mine Pick
info.minepick.intro: Mine Pick is a daily mini-game. Ten boosters are simulated every day with your real draw settings, and you see their contents before choosing. Open the pack you want, turn its cards over, then keep the one you like.
info.minepick.step1: Every booster on the board is drawn exactly like a real one: same rarity table, same number of cards and the same god pack rate (five full art printings).
info.minepick.step2: The board is computed from the UTC date and your identifier: it does not change before midnight UTC, and it is yours alone.
info.minepick.step3: Three free picks a day, reset at midnight UTC. They are independent from the three free daily boosters.
info.minepick.step4: A booster you already picked from stays listed with the card you kept: that card joins the collection and feeds the Mine Pick counters of the statistics.
info.minepick.help: Mine Pick consumes no booster: it simulates the openings of the day, and only one card is kept per pick.
info.keyboard.title: Keyboard controls
info.keyboard.intro: Mouse and touch are enough everywhere. These shortcuts speed up the Mine and the closing of dialogs.
info.keyboard.hold: Keep mining while the combo is held.
info.keyboard.trader: Open the Wandering Trader from the Mine.
info.keyboard.escape: Close the open dialog (shop, inventory, card detail).
info.keyboard.help: Shortcuts are ignored while the cursor is in a text field or on another button: they never steal a keystroke.
info.mining.title: Mine
info.mining.intro: The Mine gives a daily quota of blocks, reset at midnight UTC. Every block takes several hits before it breaks, then drops its resources.
info.mining.step1: Tap the block, or press Space, to land a hit: the crack shows the damage already dealt.
info.mining.step2: Hold Shift + Space to chain hits without releasing the keys.
info.mining.step3: A broken block gives its dust, sometimes Sparks. Harvested resources gather in the chest inventory.
info.mining.step4: Resources are spent at the Wandering Trader: they pay for his cards or are swapped between each other.
info.mining.help: The blocks, their hardness and their loot live in the game configuration files: their daily order belongs to each account.
info.trader.title: Wandering Trader
info.trader.intro: The Wandering Trader opens from the Mine, with its button or the S key. He sells cards for the resources you harvest.
info.trader.step1: The pinned card is hand-written: it opens the shop, with its own sale window and stock.
info.trader.step2: The five cards of the week are the same for every player and change on Monday at midnight UTC. Their price is paid in three resources whose total value matches the rarity of the card.
info.trader.step3: Daily trades exchange one resource for another of equal value, once per day and per trade.
info.trader.step4: A daily offer sells one resource for Sparks: the quantity is drawn at random within a value cap set by the configuration, and its price is twice that value.
info.trader.help: Everything the trader sells returns at midnight UTC for daily offers, and on Monday for the cards of the week.
info.experience.title: Experience and levels
info.experience.intro: Your profile earns experience at every step of the game. That total is never spent: it only grows, and your level follows.
info.about.title: About MineCards
info.about.intro: MineCards is a collectible card game inspired by the Minecraft universe, free and playable in your browser. You get three free boosters every day and per expansion, each one holding 5 cards drawn with the rates published below.
info.about.collection: The Genesis expansion (A1) gathers 222 cards in five rarities: Common, Rare, Super rare, Legendary and Mythic, in classic or Full Art printing. Every card you pull joins your collection. Duplicates can be sold for Sparks, enough to buy the card you are still missing.
info.experience.card: Every distinct card in your collection
info.about.local: No sign-up is required and nothing is sent to a server: your collection, Sparks and statistics stay in your browser, and a save file can be exported and imported again.
info.experience.name: A custom player name
info.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
info.faq.q1: Is MineCards an official Minecraft game?
info.faq.a1: No. MineCards is an unofficial collectible card game made by enthusiasts: it is neither published nor endorsed by Mojang or Microsoft. The card artwork comes from the Minecraft universe and is credited on this page.
info.experience.levelText: Level {next} needs {base} XP, then every further level asks for {increment} XP more than the previous one.
info.faq.q2: How many free boosters can be opened each day?
info.faq.a2: Three free boosters per day and per expansion. Bonus boosters can be added through promo codes and distributions; they stack without limit until opened.
info.experience.help: These values come straight from the game configuration: this is exactly the experience you earn.
info.accountValue.title: Points
info.accountValue.intro: Account value, shown as “Points”, is a progression indicator expressed in theoretical Sparks. It can never be spent or withdrawn.
info.accountValue.cards: The sale value of every owned copy in the collection, by rarity (10 Sparks for a promo card).
info.accountValue.distinct: For every distinct owned card, its rarity cubed multiplied by 10: a Common (rarity 1) adds 10, a Mythic (rarity 5) adds 1,250.
info.accountValue.resources: Each mined resource quantity multiplied by its Wandering Trader value.
info.accountValue.currencies: Each custom currency balance multiplied by 25.
info.accountValue.boosters: Each bonus booster multiplied by the booster shop price.
info.accountValue.bundles: Each block bundle multiplied by its shop price.
info.accountValue.customizations: Each purchased profile customisation (Full Art, colours, avatar, size, anchor, slot) valued at its Sparks price, at one point per Spark.
info.accountValue.help: Prices and values are read from the game configuration. Account value is recalculated from the account and never stored as a balance. From one million, the display is abbreviated with two truncated decimals: 1.43 M, then 1.43 B.
info.faq.q3: How many cards does the Genesis expansion contain?
info.faq.a3: The Genesis expansion (A1) contains 222 cards across five rarities: Common, Rare, Super rare, Legendary and Mythic, in classic printing (197 cards) or Full Art (25 cards). Every booster holds 5 cards.
info.faq.q4: Do I need an account, or need to pay, to play?
info.faq.a4: No: the game is entirely free and asks for no sign-up. An account identifier is created locally in your browser; the collection, Sparks and statistics stay on the device, and a save file can be exported and imported again.
info.faq.a5: Sparks are the game's currency: every booster you open grants a few, and duplicate cards can be sold according to their rarity. They are then used to buy a specific card straight from the collection.
info.faq.a6: Occasionally, a booster can be a godpack: all five of its cards are then Full Art printings, whatever their rarity.

view.titles.title: Title
view.titles.help: A title is the line shown under your pseudo. It is unlocked by gaining a level or by completing a collection; once unlocked, it is picked here - or not displayed at all.
view.titles.subtitle: Pick the title shown under your pseudo: one row per title, greyed out until it is unlocked.

error.popup.title: Something went wrong
error.popup.body: The game ran into a problem. The report holds everything needed to understand what happened: copy it and send it on Discord or GitHub.
error.popup.bodyReload: If it shows up right after an update, it may come from files that are not up to date yet: reload the page (Ctrl+F5), that is often all it takes.
error.popup.copyFailed: The copy was refused: select the text of the details above.
error.popup.hint: Every button copies the whole report; the last two also open Discord or GitHub in a new tab. Paste it in the help channel or in an issue.
error.popup.body3d: The booster is shown in 2D. Copy the error code: it holds your browser, your graphics card and the WebGL renderer in use, which is what finds the cause.
error.popup.titleImage: An image could not be loaded
error.popup.bodyImage: The game goes on without it. Copy the error code: it holds the address of the image and the browser in use.
error.popup.bodyBoot: Copy the error code before reloading: it holds what blocked the start-up. If the game was just updated, a file that is not up to date yet may be the cause: a simple reload of the page (Ctrl+F5) often fixes it.
